system.description:
Not every ranger works alone. Some build a partnership with the wild, starting with whatever creature will have them, and in time earning the trust of things that shouldn't trust anyone.

  • Bonded Companion (1st): tame and bond with a beast companion that fights and travels with you: at 1st level a mundane animal suited to the terrain (wolf, hawk, boar), bonded over a few days of feeding and handling, with HD equal to half your Ranger level (rounded up).
  • It acts on its own initiative and defends itself and you whenever either of you is threatened, at no cost to you.
  • Directing it to attack a particular target or do a particular thing costs your action.
  • Beastspeaker (1st): Advantage on checks to calm, speak with or avoid provoking wild animals and beast-type monsters, even ones far beyond what you could safely fight. It grants no control over an unbonded creature.
  • Wild Bond (5th): you may try to tame a beast-type monster of low power (giant spider, dire wolf or similar, GM-approved). Taming takes days of exposure and a Wisdom check the GM sets by the creature's HD and temper, and can fail or provoke an attack.
  • Apex Bond (10th): you may try the same with a dangerous beast-type monster (a young wyvern, a manticore or a similar apex predator, GM-approved); failure is likely to mean a fight. If a bonded companion is slain, a replacement of the right tier can be found after a season of searching.
